summary: Single deployable monolith: React (Vite SPA) (web) on Python 3.13 + Django 5.2 LTS with Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL 17, hosted on Google Cloud Run. Estimated $10-50/month.

frontend.justification: Web: React (Vite SPA) — Rich interactive app screens.

alternatives.why_not: React (Vite SPA) is stronger on: good fast delivery (priority 3/5) (priorities.time_to_market). Overall 2.4 points behind. Known limit of Vue 3: smaller hiring pool and component ecosystem than React.

React (Vite SPA) is stronger on: rich interactive app screens (project.type); good low running cost (priority 3/5) (priorities.cost). Overall 3.5 points behind. Known limit of Blazor: smaller component ecosystem than React.

tradeoffs: Client-rendered pages are weak for SEO

backend.justification: Team already writes python for the API.

alternatives.why_not: Python 3.13 + Django 5.2 LTS is stronger on: good maintainability (priority 3/5) (priorities.maintainability); good security (priority 3/5) (priorities.security). Overall 3.6 points behind. Known limit of Python 3.13 + FastAPI: bring-your-own admin/auth pieces.

Team lists python but this needs typescript/javascript (team.languages). Python 3.13 + Django 5.2 LTS is stronger on: good security (priority 3/5) (priorities.security). Overall 14.3 points behind. Known limit of Node.js 24 LTS + NestJS: more boilerplate than Express.

what_would_change.new_choice: No single-field edit among the probed priorities, requirements, numbers and constraints changes this choice.

database.justification: Best overall fit for the stated inputs.

alternatives.why_not: Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL 17 is stronger on: good maintainability (priority 3/5) (priorities.maintainability); good security (priority 3/5) (priorities.security). Overall 4.8 points behind. Known limit of Cloud SQL for MySQL 8.4: 8.0 moved to Sustaining Support (Apr 2026); no row-level security.

Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL 17 is stronger on: good maintainability (priority 3/5) (priorities.maintainability); good low running cost (priority 3/5) (priorities.cost). Overall 5.2 points behind. Known limit of Cloud Firestore: no joins or full-text search; aggregations are limited.
Excluded: a separate vendor outside the explicit cloud_preference gcp (infrastructure.cloud_preference).

tradeoffs: Vertical write scaling; sharding needs extensions

hosting.justification: Satisfies the hard constraints (cloud_preference gcp, managed_cloud (no servers to patch)). Fully managed runtime (patching, TLS, scaling handled) for a team without a DevOps person; quick to set up for a 4-week MVP.

alternatives.why_not: Excluded: runs on azure, but cloud_preference is gcp (infrastructure.cloud_preference).
Excluded: runs on azure, but cloud_preference is gcp (infrastructure.cloud_preference).
Excluded: runs on render, but cloud_preference is gcp (infrastructure.cloud_preference).

tradeoffs: Cold starts unless min instances are paid for
Per-request timeout bounds long jobs and WebSocket connections (clients must reconnect)

what_would_change.new_choice: AWS Elastic Beanstalk (managed platform on EC2)

supporting.justification: email_password login kept inside the application: users live in your own database, so no extra vendor or data transfer.

alternatives.why_not: extra monthly cost per active user and identity data outside your region
a separate service to run for a single application

tradeoffs: You own password hashing, reset e-mails and MFA setup

supporting.justification: Automated tests and deploys on every push to Google Cloud Run; free minutes cover a team of 1.

alternatives.why_not: equivalent; GitHub chosen for its marketplace of deploy actions

tradeoffs: Secrets must be stored as encrypted environment secrets

supporting.justification: Logs and metrics stay with the host provider; alerts on error rate and latency.

alternatives.why_not: extra vendor; add later for richer error grouping

tradeoffs: Log retention costs grow with traffic

supporting.justification: Reminders and other timed work run from a scheduler that calls the app on a schedule, so no always-on process or hand-rolled timer loop is needed.

alternatives.why_not: lost on every restart or deploy; duplicated across instances

tradeoffs: Make scheduled jobs idempotent: a schedule can fire twice

assumptions: Hosting Google Cloud Run: $0-10/month at the 'tiny' tier.
Excluded: taxes, domain names, paid support plans and data-egress spikes. Order-of-magnitude band, not a quote.

warnings.message: Upper estimate $50/month can exceed the $20 budget at peak usage.

assumptions: requirements.p95_latency_ms absent or null: no explicit latency target; typical web latency assumed.
Knowledge base as of 2026-11-11; lifecycle and pricing judgements use that date, not the run date.
Scale tier 'tiny' from 10 users and ~3 peak concurrent users (people, not requests per second; used only for sizing and cost).
No data_residency given: deploy in the provider region closest to most users (not specified in the input).
